title: Presence policy enforced only on audience[0] while all audiences are signed into the SVID
description:
EXPLOITABLE NOW. Presence-requirement bypass by audience ordering.

persona-grpc/src/service.rs:113 parses persona_ extensions from the FIRST audience only:
    let ext = AudienceExtensions::parse(&req.audience[0])?;
service.rs:146-153 checks ext.require_presence against the claim. But service.rs:176 signs the token for EVERY audience the caller supplied:
    let audiences: Vec<&str> = req.audience.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();

TRIGGER: call FetchJWTSVID with
    audience = ["https://harmless.example",
                "https://bank.example?persona_require_presence=hardware"]
Element [0] parses to require_presence = None, so the check at service.rs:146 passes with a PresenceLevel::None claim. The issued token carries both strings in aud.

CONSEQUENCE: the relying party at bank.example receives a validly signed JWT-SVID whose aud matches the exact audience string it published, including its own persona_require_presence=hardware policy marker, for a subject whose presence was never attested at hardware level (or at all). ValidateJWTSVID (service.rs:224) matches aud by string equality, so it accepts it too. The attacker gets a credential for a presence-gated audience without satisfying the gate.

Second, related defect at the same site: ext.audience - the bare URL with persona_ params stripped (persona-core/src/audience.rs:73-77) - is computed and then discarded. The raw, unstripped strings are what get signed, so the aud claim carries policy parameters rather than the audience identifier, and a relying party matching on the bare URL will reject its own tokens.

Fix direction: parse every element of req.audience, require the STRONGEST presence level across all of them, and sign ext.audience (the stripped form) rather than the raw request strings.
